overclaims: The 2023 report also describes stronger performance by another model; that does not negate persistence of failures.
checks.note: The proposition ('LLMs' failure at chess world models') takes the world-model reading that the contract flagged as ambiguous, and it widens 'not just ChatGPT' to LLMs in general. The 'supported' outcome rests only on the behavioural reading (illegal moves), and the rationale and limitations say the world-model reading is not established or remains unresolved. So the headline overstates the result. The limitation about another model's 'stronger performance' is not shown in e1's quoted text, which cuts off at 'it deserves'.

The excerpt is verbatim, including the original typo 'simply'. The attribution to Gleave and the jailbreak qualifier are shown. e1 supports Opus 4, more than 15 pages and six hours of red-teaming, and e2 (May 22, 2025) supports the weapons prohibition. The limitations correctly note there is no replication and the tested configuration is unknown. Minor: the limitation calls Gleave the 'originating researcher', but his colleague ran the test. This is not material to the outcome.

'Unresolved' matches the agreed assessment. The rationale correctly separates behavioural failures (e1: o3/o4-mini, May 2025) from the representation claim, and says specialised models show board representations, citing the probes and interventions in e2 (2024). The limitation correctly says both items predate the inferred June 2025 window. Dates and publishers are correct. The evidence excerpts are short but accurate quotes.
